subject: superb lyrebird
title: This Bird Moves 155 Tonnes of Soil a Year, More Than Any Land Animal

scenes.text: The world's greatest earth-mover on land isn't a worm. It's a bird.
The superb lyrebird is famous for copying sounds. That's not its real superpower.
It rakes the forest floor with huge clawed feet, hunting insects and other small animals.
Scientists measured it. Lyrebirds turn over about 155 tonnes of soil and leaves per hectare, every year.
Earthworms manage about 100. Gophers and moles, only 10 to 20.
So the best singer in the forest is also its biggest digger.

description:
Superb lyrebirds move more soil than any other land animal, about 155 tonnes per hectare each year.
A La Trobe University study in Ecological Applications found they out-dig earthworms, gophers and moles while raking the forest floor for food.
Did you know lyrebirds did anything besides mimic sounds?
first_comment: A single lyrebird can shift about 11 dump trucks' worth of soil and litter in a year. Which animal did you think was the biggest digger?
